**No.** `CatalogApi.CreateItem` does not publish `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent` — it publishes no integration events at all.

**Exactly what `CreateItem` does** (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:366-388`):

1. Constructs a new `CatalogItem` from the posted `product`, copying `Id`, `CatalogBrandId`, `CatalogTypeId`, `Description`, `PictureFileName`, `Price`, `AvailableStock`, `RestockThreshold`, and `MaxStockThreshold` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:370-381`).
2. Computes and assigns an AI embedding via `services.CatalogAI.GetEmbeddingAsync(item)` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:382`).
3. Adds the item to `services.Context.CatalogItems` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:384`).
4. Calls `services.Context.SaveChangesAsync()` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:385`).
5. Returns `TypedResults.Created($"/api/catalog/items/{item.Id}")` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:387`).

Its full set of outgoing calls is exactly those four: `ICatalogAI.GetEmbeddingAsync`, the `CatalogServices`/`CatalogContext` collection `Add`, and `CatalogContext.SaveChangesAsync` — no `EventService`, no `PublishThroughEventBusAsync` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:382-385`).

**Where the event actually is published:** `UpdateItem`, and only when the price actually changed — it constructs `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent(catalogItem.Id, productToUpdate.Price, priceEntry.OriginalValue)` inside an `if (priceEntry.IsModified)` guard (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:347-350`), saves it transactionally with `SaveEventAndCatalogContextChangesAsync` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:353`), then calls `services.EventService.PublishThroughEventBusAsync(priceChangedEvent)` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:356`). If the price is unchanged it just saves (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:360`).
